Integration by Meijer G functions

Source: R/integrals-meijerint.R
meijerint_indefinite.Rd

Ports of SymPy's meijerint_indefinite, meijerint_definite and meijerint_inversion (sympy/integrals/meijerint.py). The integrand is rewritten as a product of Meijer G functions, which are integrated with the formulas of Prudnikov, Brychkov and Marichev and then expanded back to elementary and special functions with hyperexpand().

Usage

meijerint_indefinite(f, x)

meijerint_definite(f, x, a, b)

meijerint_inversion(f, x, t)

Arguments

f

The integrand.

x

The integration variable.

a, b

The limits.

t

The variable of the inverse Laplace transform.

Value

An expression, a list (value, condition), or NULL.

Details

meijerint_indefinite(f, x) returns an antiderivative (possibly a Piecewise) or NULL. meijerint_definite(f, x, a, b) returns a list of the value and its convergence condition, or NULL. meijerint_inversion(f, x, t) computes the inverse Laplace transform of f, or NULL.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x")
meijerint_indefinite(sin(x), x)
#> -cos(x)
meijerint_definite(exp(-x^2), x, 0, oo)
#> [[1]]
#> sqrt(pi)/2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> True
#>
